counts <- read.table("row_count_data.nodup.txt", header=TRUE, row.names=1)
sample.info <- read.table("sample_groups.txt", header=TRUE, row.names=1)

# being sure about correct ordering

sample.info <- sample.info[colnames(counts), ]
all(colnames(counts) == rownames(sample.info))
## [1] TRUE
head(sample.info)
##             Group Patient
## S02_Normal Normal     S02
## S03_Normal Normal     S03
## S05_Normal Normal     S05
## S06_Normal Normal     S06
## S10_Normal Normal     S10
## S02_Tumour Tumour     S02
str(sample.info)
## 'data.frame':    10 obs. of  2 variables:
##  $ Group  : chr  "Normal" "Normal" "Normal" "Normal" ...
##  $ Patient: chr  "S02" "S03" "S05" "S06" ...
colnames(sample.info)
## [1] "Group"   "Patient"
# Factor setup
sample.info$Group <- factor(sample.info$Group, 
                            levels=c("Normal", "Tumour"))
sample.info$Patient <- factor(sample.info$Patient)

# DESeq object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData=counts,
                              colData=sample.info,
                              design = ~Patient + Group)

# Filter:
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 2
dds <- dds[keep, ]

# Run DESeq normalization
dds <- DESeq(dds)
## estimating size factors
## estimating dispersions
## gene-wise dispersion estimates
## mean-dispersion relationship
## final dispersion estimates
## fitting model and testing
# Extract normalized counts
normalizeddata <- counts(dds, normalized=TRUE)

normalizeddata_log <- log2(normalizeddata + 1)

# QC boxplot
boxplot(normalizeddata_log, outline=FALSE, las=2, main="Normalized expression")

# xCell (individual method), logged values
library(xCell)
est_xcell <- xCellAnalysis(normalizeddata_log)
## [1] "Num. of genes: 8827"
## ℹ GSVA version 2.4.5

dim(est_xcell)
## [1] 67 10
heatmap(est_xcell, col=colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100), main="xCell Heatmap")

#MCPcounter (individual method), logged values
library(MCPcounter)
est_mcp <- MCPcounter.estimate(normalizeddata_log, featuresType="HUGO_symbols")
dim(est_mcp)
## [1] 10 10
heatmap(as.matrix(est_mcp), col=colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100), main="MCPcounter Heatmap")

#Decosus (consensus method),  unlogged values
library(Decosus)
exp_dataun <- as.data.frame(normalizeddata)
exp_dataun$Gene <- rownames(exp_dataun)
exp_dataun <- exp_dataun[, c("Gene", colnames(normalizeddata))]

est_Decos <- Decosus::cosDeco(x = exp_dataun, rnaseq = T, plot = TRUE)
## [1] "Num. of genes: 8827"
## ℹ GSVA version 2.4.5
## ℹ Searching for rows with constant values
## ! Some gene sets have size one. Consider setting minSize > 1
## ℹ Calculating ssGSEA scores for 489 gene sets
## ℹ Calculating ranks
## ℹ Calculating rank weights
## ✔ Calculations finished
## 
## Setting helper functions for quanTIseq
## 
## Running quanTIseq deconvolution module
## Gene expression normalization and re-annotation (arrays: FALSE)
## Removing 17 noisy genes
## Signature genes found in data set: 131/153 (85.62%)
## Mixture deconvolution (method: lsei)
est_Decos_c <- est_Decos$main_cells
est_Decos_s <- est_Decos$main_samples


est_Decos_c <- as.matrix(est_Decos_c)
est_Decos_c[is.nan(est_Decos_c)] <- NA
est_Decos_c[is.na(est_Decos_c)] <- 0

heatmap(as.matrix(est_Decos_c), col=colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100), main = "Decosus Consensus Heatmap")

To get a clear picture of the cell types in our samples, we used three different tools: xCell, MCPcounter, and Decosus.we fed xCell and MCPcounter the log-transformed data, but kept the data unlogged for Decosus to make sure the results stayed accurate.

The cellular profiles created a clear split in our heatmaps, with samples clustering naturally by their type. We saw a consistent trend across all methods: tumor samples grouped together and were much richer in immune-related signatures than the normal samples. Specifically, the MCPcounter results highlighted a notable spike in T cells, CD8+ T cells, NK cells, and cytotoxic activity within the tumor environment.

To double-check, we looked at the Decosus results, that shows even steadier patterns. This consistency means confidence in the findings. it confirms that the immune activity in these tumors is a solid and reliable across the board.

Q2:

#student t-test
group <- sample.info$Group

# xCell 

pvalues_xcell <- apply(est_xcell, 1, function(x){
  t.test(x[group=="Tumour"], 
         x[group=="Normal"])$p.value})

significant_xcell <- names(pvalues_xcell[pvalues_xcell < 0.05])
significant_xcell
## [1] "Adipocytes"                    "Class-switched memory B-cells"
## [3] "Preadipocytes"                 "Tregs"
#MCPcounter
pvalues_mcp <- apply(est_mcp, 1, function(x){
  t.test(x[group=="Tumour"], 
         x[group=="Normal"])$p.value})

significant_mcp <- names(pvalues_mcp[pvalues_mcp < 0.05])
significant_mcp
## character(0)
#Decosus

pvalues_decos <- apply(est_Decos_c, 1, function(x){
  t.test(x[group=="Tumour"], 
         x[group=="Normal"])$p.value})

significant_decos <- names(pvalues_decos[pvalues_decos < 0.05])
significant_decos
## [1] NA                               "uncharacterized cell_consensus"
## [3] "Tregs_quanTISeq"
# xCell
for(cell in significant_xcell){
  boxplot(est_xcell[cell, ] ~ group, 
          main=paste(cell, "(xCell)"), 
          col=c("#5DADE2", "#EB984E"), 
          ylab="Cell enrichment score")
}

#Decosus


significant_decos <- names(pvalues_decos[!is.na(pvalues_decos) & pvalues_decos < 0.05])


for(cell_name in significant_decos){
  boxplot(est_Decos_c[cell_name, ] ~ group, 
          main = paste(cell_name, "(Decosus)"),
          col = c("#5DADE2", "#EB984E"), 
          ylab = "Cell enrichment score",
          las = 1) 
}

we performed a Student’s t-test to compare cellular estimates between the two groups(tumour and normal samples). The xCell analysis highlighted four specific cell types that reached statistical significance with p-values less than 0.05: Adipocytes, Class-switched memory B-cells, Preadipocytes, and Tregs. (cell populations that are shifting most significantly in the tumor environment).

t-tests on the Decosus data identified two cell types with significant shifts: uncharacterized cell_consensus and Tregs_quanTISeq (p < 0.05). On the other hand, the MCPcounter analysis was less definitive; no cell types reached statistical significance at the p < 0.05 level.

#  GSVA analysis
KEGG_s <- getGmt("c2.cp.kegg.v2022.1.Hs.symbols.gmt")
class(KEGG_s)
## [1] "GeneSetCollection"
## attr(,"package")
## [1] "GSEABase"
param <- gsvaParam(expr = as.matrix(normalizeddata_log),
                   geneSets = KEGG_s,
                   kcdf = "Gaussian")

Gsva_es <- gsva(param)
## ℹ GSVA version 2.4.5
## ℹ Searching for rows with constant values
## ℹ Calculating GSVA ranks
## ℹ GSVA dense (classical) algorithm
## ℹ Row-wise ECDF estimation with Gaussian kernels
## ℹ Calculating row ECDFs
## ℹ Calculating column ranks
## ℹ GSVA dense (classical) algorithm
## ℹ Calculating GSVA scores
## ✔ Calculations finished
dim(Gsva_es)
## [1] 186  10
design <- model.matrix(~ Patient + Group, data=sample.info)
fit <- lmFit(Gsva_es, design)
fit_1 <- eBayes(fit)
gsva_kegg_results <- topTable(fit_1, coef="GroupTumour", adjust="BH", n=Inf)

# list top 10 mostly significantly differential expression KEGG pathway
significant_pathways <- rownames(gsva_kegg_results)[gsva_kegg_results$adj.P.Val <= 0.01]
length(significant_pathways)
## [1] 0
if(length(significant_pathways) >= 2){
  significant_pathways_es <- Gsva_es[significant_pathways, ]
  significant_pathways_es[is.na(significant_pathways_es)] <- 0
  heatmap(significant_pathways_es,
          scale="row",
          margins=c(5,15))}

gsva_kegg_results_sorted <- gsva_kegg_results[order(gsva_kegg_results$adj.P.Val), ]
top10 <- head(gsva_kegg_results_sorted, 10)
top10

# heatmap for mostly significantly differentially regulated KEGG
top10_list <- rownames(gsva_kegg_results)[1:10]

While no pathways met our initial, strict significance p-adj ≤ 0.01, we examined the top 10 ranked pathways to identify potential trends. These were focused on metabolic processes(carbohydrate, lipid, and steroid hormone metabolism).The majority displayed negative log fold change values, which means a general reduction in metabolic enrichment in the tumor samples. This distinction between the two groups was further confirmed by the heatmap, highlighting the difference pathway enrichment patterns between tumour and normal samples
